title: 6-hydroxygenistein attenuates hypoxia-induced injury via activating Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway in PC12 cells.
authors: Zhang, Pengpeng; Zhang, Jie; Ma, Chuan; Ma, Huiping; Jing, Linlin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究6-OHG通过Nrf2/HO-1通路缓解PC12细胞缺氧损伤，核心为小分子抗氧化机制与细胞实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: 4',5,6,7-tetrahydoxyisoflavone (6-hydroxygenistein, 6-OHG) is a hydroxylated derivative of genistein with excellent antioxidant activity, but whether 6-OHG can protect hypoxia-induced damage is unclear. The objective of current study was to evaluate the protective effect and underling mechanism of 6-OHG against hypoxia-induced injury via network pharmacology and cellular experiments. 6-OHG-related and hypoxia injury-related targets were screened by public databases. The intersected targets were used for constructing PPI network and performing GO and KEGG functional analysis. We induced injury in PC12 cells under hypoxia conditions and observed the effects and molecular mechanisms of 6-OHG on cellular damage. Network pharmacological analysis predicted that 6-OHG delayed hypoxia injury by mitigating oxidative stress, inflammatory response and apoptosis. Cellular experiments suggested that 6-OHG treatment mitigated cell damage, enhanced cell viability, reduced ROS production and MDA level, increased SOD and CAT activities and elevated GSH level in PC12 cell exposed to hypoxia. Additionally, 6-OHG treatment reduced the TNF-alpha and IL-6 levels and elevated the IL-10 content, while downregulated the NF-kappaB and TNF-alpha expressions. 6-OHG also inhibited the caspase-3 and - 9 activation and the Bax and cleaved caspase-3 expressions, and elevated the Bcl-2 expression. Moreover, 6-OHG remarkably enhanced Nrf2 nuclear translocation and increased HO-1 expression. Molecular docking also proved the strong binding affinities of 6-OHG with Nrf2 and HO-1. Furthermore, ML385, a specific Nrf2 inhibitor, eliminated the beneficial effects of 6-OHG. In summary, 6-OHG can alleviate hypoxia-induced injury in PC12 cells through activating Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway and may be developed as candidate for preventing neuro-damage induced by hypoxia.
abstract_zh: 4',5,6,7-四羟基异黄酮（6-氢金雀异黄酮，6-OHG）是金雀异黄酮的一种羟基化衍生物，具有优异的抗氧化活性，但6-OHG是否能保护缺氧诱导的损伤尚不清楚。本研究旨在通过网络药理学和细胞实验评估6-OHG对缺氧诱导损伤的保护作用及其潜在机制。通过公共数据库筛选了与6-OHG相关和缺氧损伤相关的靶点。交集靶点用于构建PPI网络并进行GO和KEGG功能分析。我们在缺氧条件下诱导PC12细胞损伤，并观察6-OHG对细胞损伤的作用及分子机制。网络药理学分析预测，6-OHG通过缓解氧化应激、炎症反应和细胞凋亡来延缓缺氧损伤。细胞实验表明，6-OHG处理减轻了缺氧暴露的PC12细胞的细胞损伤，增强了细胞活力，降低了ROS产生和MDA水平，增加了SOD和CAT活性，并提高了GSH水平。此外，6-OHG处理降低了TNF-alpha和IL-6水平，提高了IL-10含量，同时下调了NF-kappaB和TNF-alpha的表达。6-OHG还抑制了caspase-3和caspase-9的激活以及Bax和cleaved caspase-3的表达，并提高了Bcl-2的表达。此外，6-OHG显著增强了Nrf2核转位并增加了HO-1表达。分子对接也证明了6-OHG与Nrf2和HO-1的强结合亲和力。进一步地，ML385（一种特异性Nrf2抑制剂）消除了6-OHG的有益效应。总之，6-OHG通过激活Nrf2/HO-1信号通路减轻缺氧诱导的PC12细胞损伤，并可能被开发为预防缺氧诱导神经损伤的候选药物。
